mainTopic: Torah sources for valid סכך, and why tied bundles may not be used as סכך.
overview: The גמרא first looks for a פסוק behind the rule that סכך must grow from the ground and must not be able to receive טומאה. It rejects comparing סוכה to the חגיגה offering, since an offering is an animal. רבין, in the name of רבי יוחנן, reads 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך' as speaking about the leftover waste of the threshing floor and winepress. רבי זירא defends this reading because you cannot roof with wine, but רבי ירמיה knocks that down with congealed wine. רב אשי then saves the proof: 'from' your threshing floor means what comes out of it, not the produce itself. רב חסדא brings a second source, the branches listed in נחמיה, and explains why both הדס and עץ עבות are mentioned. A new משנה rules that tied bundles may not be used as סכך. The גמרא matches the bundles rule to גזירת אוצר and the hollowed grain stack to תעשה ולא מן העשוי. רב אשי challenges that split, and רבי יוחנן's defense from the משנה's wording begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the סוכה is compared to the חגיגה offering, it would have to be made of animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier source that learned סוכה from חגיגה. Taken all the way, that comparison would require the סוכה to be made of animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as the חגיגה offering is an animal, the סוכה should also be made from animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the source suggested on the previous amud, which linked the סוכה to the חגיגה (festival offering). It shows that this comparison leads to an absurd result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source said the סוכה is like the חגיגה, so the סכך should share the חגיגה's qualities. But the most obvious quality of a חגיגה is that it is a living animal. Since no one makes סכך out of animals, the comparison collapses as a source.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your source is correct)
The festival peace-offering brought on יום טוב

steps.confusionAlert: This line refers back to a source given on the previous amud, the comparison of סוכה to חגיגה. It is not a new idea. It is a challenge that knocks down the previous attempt.

phrases.english: If so: just as the festival offering is animals,
phrases.notes: 'מה... אף...' is the classic pattern for drawing a comparison.

phrases.english: so too the sukkah should also be animals!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי: מָה חֲגִיגָה בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים, אַף סוּכָּה נָמֵי בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source proposed earlier on the daf, on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation comparing סוכה to חגיגה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would force the סכך to share the חגיגה's defining trait, being an animal, which is absurd.

steps.title: A new source: the verse speaks of the leftovers of the threshing floor and winepress
steps.stepSummary: רבין brings, in the name of רבי יוחנן, a new source from the פסוק 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך'. The פסוק is about the leftover waste of the threshing floor and winepress, which grows from the ground and cannot receive טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The פסוק says, 'When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress.' The פסוק is speaking about the waste of the threshing floor and the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: With the earlier source knocked down, the גמרא brings a brand new one. It says the סוכה is roofed with the leftovers from harvesting grain and grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about סוכות mentions the threshing floor and the winepress. רבי יוחנן reads it as pointing to their waste: straw, stalks and vine branches. These grow from the ground and are not food or vessels, so they cannot receive טומאה. That matches the משנה's rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Threshing floor, where grain is separated

steps.whyThisMatters: This source fits both halves of the משנה's rule at once: it grows from the ground, and it does not receive טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
the verse states: 'When you gather from your threshing floor and from your winepress,'
phrases.notes: דברים טז:יג, in the passage about חג הסוכות.

phrases.english: it is about the waste of the threshing floor and winepress that the verse speaks.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך' teaches that סכך is made from the waste of the threshing floor and winepress.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the actual grain and grapes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading of the פסוק. Perhaps it means the produce itself, which is food and can receive טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it means the threshing floor itself and the winepress itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's reading. It asks why the פסוק could not mean the real contents of the threshing floor and winepress, the grain and the grapes or wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק means the produce itself, then it is talking about food. Food can receive טומאה, so the פסוק would no longer support the משנה's rule. The challenge is: what forces us to read 'waste' into the פסוק?

phrases.english: But say the threshing floor itself and the winepress itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוק given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reading of the פסוק as 'waste'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain words could mean the produce itself. Produce is food that receives טומאה, so the proof for the משנה would fail.

steps.title: You cannot roof a sukkah with wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that the פסוק says 'יקב', and the winepress holds wine. Wine cannot be used as סכך, so the פסוק must mean the waste.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: 'Winepress' is written here, and it is impossible to roof with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא defends רבי יוחנן's reading. He proves the פסוק cannot mean the actual produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The actual contents of a winepress are wine, which is a liquid. A liquid cannot be put on top of a סוכה. So the word יקב cannot refer to its contents, and the פסוק must mean the leftover vine branches. The same then applies to the גורן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: 'Winepress' is written here,
and it is impossible to roof with it.
phrases.notes: Its contents are wine, a liquid.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might mean the actual grain and wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wine cannot be used as סכך, so the פסוק must mean the waste.

steps.title: Congealed wine could be used for roofing
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה objects to רבי זירא's answer. Congealed wine from שניר is solid like a fig cake, so one could roof with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה strongly objected: But say it means congealed wine that comes from שניר, which is like cakes of pressed figs!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה attacks רבי זירא's answer. He shows that some wine is solid, so 'you cannot roof with wine' is not always true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא's whole answer depended on wine being a liquid. רבי ירמיה points to a solid, congealed wine from שניר (חרמון) that could physically be placed on a סוכה. If that is possible, the פסוק could again mean actual food, and the proof for the משנה is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: שניר, a name for Mount חרמון

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya strongly objected to it:
But say congealed wine that comes from Senir,
which is similar to cakes of pressed figs!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי זירא's answer in step 4, bringing back the challenge of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's claim that one cannot roof with wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Solid wine exists and could serve as roofing, so the פסוק could mean actual produce, which receives טומאה.

steps.title: רבי זירא admits the proof has been broken
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא concedes. He says they had the proof in hand, and רבי ירמיה came and took an axe to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: We had this matter in our hands, and רבי ירמיה came and threw an axe at it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא accepts רבי ירמיה's objection. He admits that the proof from 'יקב' no longer stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new answer. It is a colorful admission of defeat: a solid proof has been chopped down. As a result, רבי זירא's defense of the derivation from 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך' fails. The next step shows how רב אשי rescues the same פסוק in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: Was in our hands (we had it settled)
Threw an axe at it (destroyed it)

steps.whatToRemember: There have been two attempts so far. The comparison to חגיגה failed because an offering is an animal. רבי זירא's defense of the proof from גורן and יקב was undermined by congealed wine. The next step, רב אשי, restores this proof with a different reading.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not answering רבי ירמיה here. He is admitting that the objection succeeds.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: הָא מִלְּתָא הֲוָה בִּידַן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: This matter was in our hands,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וּשְׁדָא בַּיהּ נַרְגָּא.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yirmeya came and threw an axe at it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִלְּתָא הֲוָה בִּידַן, וַאֲתָא רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה וּשְׁדָא בַּיהּ נַרְגָּא
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי זירא's proof from יקב is undermined by the possibility of congealed wine. Step 7 (רב אשי) restores the source from 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך' with a different reading.

steps.title: רב אשי saves the proof from the word 'from'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads 'מגרנך' and 'מיקבך' as meaning what comes out of the threshing floor and winepress, the leftover waste, and not the produce itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: 'From your threshing floor' means something that comes out of it, not what is on the threshing floor itself. 'From your winepress' means something that comes out of it, not what is in the winepress itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a new way to defend the proof from 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך' after רבי זירא's answer fell apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 3 was that maybe the פסוק means the produce itself, which is food and can become טמא. רב אשי says the letter 'מ', meaning 'from', points to what is left over from the גורן and יקב, the waste. The produce itself is what sits on the floor or in the press, not what comes 'from' it. This answers the challenge without needing the argument about wine, so רבי ירמיה's objection no longer matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor, where grain is separated from the chaff
Winepress, or the pit where the wine collects
Itself, meaning the thing itself and not what comes out of it

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
"From your threshing floor", and not the threshing floor itself,
phrases.notes: What comes out of the floor (the waste), not what sits on it (the grain)

phrases.english: "From your winepress", and not the winepress itself.
phrases.notes: What comes out of the press (the waste), not what is in it (the grapes)

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: ״מִגׇּרְנְךָ״ וְלֹא גּוֹרֶן עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי זירא gave up his answer, רב אשי offers a different answer to the step 3 challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק might mean the produce itself, which is food and can become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'From' your threshing floor and winepress means the leftover waste, which grows from the ground and cannot become טמא.

steps.title: רב חסדא brings a source from נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a different source for valid סכך: the פסוק in נחמיה that lists the branches the people gathered to build סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said that we learn it from here: 'Go out to the mountain and bring olive branches, branches of the oil tree, myrtle branches, palm branches, and branches of the thick tree.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא offers a whole new פסוק as the source for what may be used as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In נחמיה, the people are told to bring branches and leaves in order to build סוכות. All the items listed are plant materials that grow from the ground and do not become טמא. So this list serves as a model of proper סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: From here, introducing a new source
Thick tree, a tree whose leaves cover each other

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said: from here:
"Go out to the mountain and bring
olive branches and branches of the oil tree
and myrtle branches and palm branches
and branches of the thick tree."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second, independent source alongside the פסוק of 'באספך מגרנך ומיקבך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The branches listed in נחמיה, all plants from the ground that are not מקבל טומאה, show what kind of material is valid סכך.

steps.title: Why does the verse list myrtle twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that הדס and עץ עבות seem to be the same plant, so why does the פסוק mention both?
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'myrtle' is the same thing as 'thick tree'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוק seems to repeat itself and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עץ עבות is the term the תורה uses for the myrtle of the ארבעה מינים. If הדס and עץ עבות are the same plant, listing both looks like an extra, unnecessary word.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as, used to point out an apparent repetition

phrases.english: That is "myrtle",
that is "thick tree"!
phrases.notes: They are the same plant, so why list both?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step questions the wording of the פסוק that רב חסדא just brought.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the פסוק in נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק should not list the same item twice, so the repetition needs an explanation.

steps.title: Wild myrtle for the סוכה, real myrtle for the לולב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'הדס' means a wild myrtle used for the סוכה, and 'עץ עבות' means the proper myrtle used for the לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: a wild myrtle is for the סוכה, and the thick tree is for the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question by showing that the two words refer to two different kinds of myrtle used for two different מצוות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדס שוטה, a wild myrtle, does not have the thick, layered leaves needed for the ארבעה מינים, so it was used for סכך. The עץ עבות, whose leaves cover each other, is the kosher myrtle that was gathered for the לולב. So there is no repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: Wild myrtle, one that is not valid for the ארבעה מינים
Here, the מצוה of the ארבעה מינים

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A wild myrtle is for the sukkah,
and the thick tree is for the lulav.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הֲדַס שׁוֹטֶה לְסוּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This step directly answers the question about the repetition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two kinds of myrtle used for two purposes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הדס and עץ עבות are the same item listed twice.
steps.terutzMaskana: הדס is a wild myrtle for סכך, and עץ עבות is the kosher myrtle for the לולב.
steps.whatToRemember: Two sources for valid סכך: the פסוק of 'מגרנך ומיקבך' (as read by רב אשי) and the list of branches in נחמיה.

steps.title: New משנה: tied bundles cannot be used as סכך
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that tied bundles of straw, wood, or twigs may not be used as סכך. If untied, they are valid, and even tied they are valid for the walls.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Bundles of straw, bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs may not be used as סכך. If one untied any of them, they are valid. All of them are valid for walls.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, teaching a rule about tied bundles of plant material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not the material, because straw, wood, and twigs are normal valid סכך. The problem is only that they are tied in bundles, since once untied they become valid. The rule applies only to the roof, because tied bundles are fine for the דפנות. The גמרא will explain the reason for this rule next.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think straw or wood is invalid סכך. The material is fine. Only the tied-bundle state is a problem, and only for the roof.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִין —
phrases.english: Bundles of straw, bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs:
one may not roof with them.
And all of them, if one untied them, are valid.
And all of them are valid for walls.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This begins a new משנה and a new topic, after the discussion of sources for סכך ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tied bundles of straw, wood, or twigs are invalid as סכך. Once untied they are valid, and even tied they are valid for walls.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule shows that validity of סכך depends not only on the material but also on how it is placed. This sets up the גמרא's search for the reason.

steps.title: רבי יעקב heard two rulings from רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב reports that he heard two related rulings from רבי יוחנן: the bundles rule of our משנה, and the rule that hollowing out a grain stack does not make a valid סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יעקב said: I heard two things from רבי יוחנן. One is this ruling about bundles. The other is that if someone hollows out a stack of grain to make a סוכה, it is not a valid סוכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting רבי יעקב, who heard two connected rulings from his teacher רבי יוחנן. This sets up a question about the reasons behind them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case one is our משנה: tied bundles are not valid as סכך. Case two is a later משנה: digging a space out of a pile of grain sheaves does not make a סוכה. רבי יעקב links the two cases because they share a common question about why they are not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
One who digs or hollows out

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Yaakov said:
I heard two things from Rabbi Yochanan:
One is this (the bundles ruling),
phrases.notes: Refers to our משנה about tied bundles

phrases.english: and the other: one who hollows out a stack of grain
to make himself a sukkah, it is not a sukkah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב: שְׁמַעִית מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא on the משנה of step 11 about tied bundles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן ruled on two cases: tied bundles as סכך, and a סוכה hollowed out of a grain stack, which is invalid.

steps.title: Two reasons, but which goes with which case?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב says one case is invalid because of גזירת אוצר and the other because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי. He does not remember which reason belongs to which case.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is because of the rabbinic decree about a storehouse. The other is because the Torah says 'make' a סוכה, and not use something already made. But I do not know which one is because of the storehouse and which one is because of 'make, and not from what is already made.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב gives two reasons for the two cases but admits he forgot which reason goes with which. This sets up a puzzle for the next step to solve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two very different kinds of reason here. גזירת אוצר is a rabbinic safeguard: the סוכה might really be fine, but the Rabbis banned it so people would not confuse it with a storage shed. תעשה ולא מן העשוי is a Torah-level rule: a סוכה must be actively made, and you cannot use something that was already standing there.

keyTerms.meaning: The rabbinic decree about a storehouse, made so a person does not use a storage shed as a סוכה
'You shall make,' and not from what is already made. A סוכה must be actively prepared.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two reasons. גזירת אוצר is only a rabbinic safeguard. תעשה ולא מן העשוי is a Torah rule about how a סוכה must be made.

phrases.english: One is because of the decree of the storehouse.
And one is because of: 'You shall make,' and not from what is already made.
But I do not know
which of them is because of the storehouse

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ מִשּׁוּם תַּעֲשֶׂה וְלֹא מִן הֶעָשׂוּי.
phrases.english: and which of them is because of 'make, and not from what is already made.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two reasons for the cases in step 12 and raises an open doubt about which reason fits which case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case (bundles or grain stack) is based on גזירת אוצר, and which is based on תעשה ולא מן העשוי?

steps.title: רבי ירמיה brings רבי יוחנן's explanation of the bundles rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה quotes רבי יוחנן through רבי חייא בר אבא. The bundles rule exists because a person might leave a bundle to dry on his shed and later decide to use it as סכך, and that would break תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Let us look into it. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Why did the Rabbis say that bundles of straw, wood, or twigs may not be used as סכך? Because sometimes a person comes home from the field in the evening with his bundle on his shoulder. He puts it on top of his shed to dry, and later he decides to use it as סכך. But the Torah said: 'Make' it, and not from what is already made.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה tries to solve רבי יעקב's doubt. He brings a statement of רבי יוחנן that explains why bundles are not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bundle in this story was put on the shed only to dry, not to be סכך, so the shed works like a storehouse. Using that shed as a סוכה without doing anything new would break the Torah rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי. The Rabbis therefore banned all tied bundles, so that people would not end up in this storehouse situation.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us look into it and figure it out
And he changes his mind or reconsiders

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן does mention the Torah rule 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי' here. But that rule applies to the storehouse situation in the story. The ban on all bundles is a rabbinic decree meant to keep people away from that situation. This is why the bundles rule counts as גזירת אוצר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said: Let us see (for ourselves),

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: for Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
For what reason did they say

phrases.aramaic: חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים וַחֲבִילֵי זְרָדִין
phrases.english: that bundles of straw, bundles of wood, and bundles of twigs
may not be used for roofing (a sukkah)?

phrases.aramaic: פְּעָמִים שֶׁאָדָם בָּא מִן הַשָּׂדֶה בָּעֶרֶב
phrases.english: Sometimes a person comes from the field in the evening
with his bundle on his shoulder,
and he lifts it up and places it on top of his shed
phrases.notes: Here 'סוכתו' means his hut or shed, not a proper סוכה

phrases.english: in order to dry it,
and then he changes his mind and decides to use it as roofing,
and the Torah said: 'You shall make,' and not from what is already made.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: נִיחְזֵי אֲנַן, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings evidence to solve the doubt raised in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the bundles rule is based on גזירת אוצר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's explanation, reported by רבי חייא בר אבא, of why bundles may not be used as סכך

steps.title: Bundles are a storehouse decree, so the grain stack is the Torah rule
steps.stepSummary: Since the bundles rule comes from גזירת אוצר, the grain-stack rule must come from תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since this one (bundles) is because of the storehouse decree, that one (the grain stack) must be because of 'make, and not from what is already made.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה finishes his proof. He matches each case to its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There were only two reasons and two cases. Once we know the bundles rule is the storehouse decree, the other reason must belong to the grain stack. Hollowing out a grain stack does not make anything new. The sheaves above were already there, so it breaks the Torah rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.whatToRemember: Tied bundles as סכך = rabbinic גזירת אוצר. Hollowing out a grain stack = Torah rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the bundles rule is only rabbinic. That explains why untied bundles, or bundles used for walls, are allowed, as the משנה ruled in step 11.

phrases.english: Since this one is because of the decree of the storehouse,
that one is because of 'You shall make,' and not from what is already made.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the evidence in step 14 and fully answers the doubt from step 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Bundles are banned because of גזירת אוצר. The hollowed grain stack is invalid because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי.

steps.title: Why didn't רבי יעקב know this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יעקב was unsure, since the answer could be worked out from רבי יוחנן's own words.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יעקב? (Why didn't he know this?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יעקב had a doubt at all if the answer was available. This sets up the short answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן had clearly explained the bundles rule. So it seems strange that רבי יעקב, his own student, could not tell which reason went with which case.

keyTerms.meaning: And רבי יעקב? (a short way of asking what he would say)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yaakov? (Why was he unsure?)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about רבי יעקב's doubt from step 13, now that step 15 solved it easily.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יעקב could not figure out the answer himself

steps.title: רבי יעקב never heard that statement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב had never heard רבי חייא בר אבא's report of רבי יוחנן's explanation, so he could not solve the doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had not heard that statement of רבי חייא בר אבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: רבי יעקב did not know the statement that solves the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on one specific report from רבי חייא בר אבא. Without it, רבי יעקב had no way to tell which reason matched which case.

phrases.english: That statement of Rabbi Chiya bar Abba
he had not heard.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָךְ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יעקב did not know רבי חייא בר אבא's report, which was the key to solving the doubt.

steps.title: רב אשי: Both reasons apply to both cases
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the split. Why should the bundles case have only גזירת אוצר and not תעשה ולא מן העשוי? And why should the grain-stack case have only תעשה ולא מן העשוי and not גזירת אוצר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Do you mean to say that bundles of straw and bundles of wood are a problem only because of גזירת אוצר, and not because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי? And in the case of one who hollows out a grain stack, is the problem only תעשה ולא מן העשוי, and not גזירת אוצר?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the conclusion of the earlier steps, which gave each case its own reason. He argues that each case should carry both reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 explained that גזירת אוצר exists because of a fear of breaking תעשה ולא מן העשוי. So that same principle is already inside the bundles case. Likewise, a grain stack is itself a store of produce, much like a storehouse, so the storehouse concern should apply there too. To רב אשי, there is no real reason to tie each reason to only one case.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? A word that opens a surprised, challenging question.
Bundles of straw and bundles of wood.
One who hollows out a stack of grain to make a סוכה.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not denying that each case is invalid. He only challenges the claim that each case has just ONE reason.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Is that to say that bundles of straw and bundles of wood
have the problem of the storehouse decree,
but not the problem of "make it, and not from what is already made"?
And one who hollows out a grain stack,
has the problem of "make it, and not from what is already made,"
but not the problem of the storehouse decree?
phrases.notes: The point: both reasons should apply to both cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַטּוּ חֲבִילֵי קַשׁ וַחֲבִילֵי עֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 15, which gave each case its own reason.
steps.kashyaTarget: The split in step 15: bundles get גזירת אוצר, and the grain stack gets תעשה ולא מן העשוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: גזירת אוצר is itself based on a fear of breaking תעשה ולא מן העשוי. So the two reasons overlap, and both should apply in both cases.

steps.title: Defending רבי יוחנן from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן could answer that the two cases are written differently in the משנה. The bundles case says "one may not roof with them," which speaks about what to do from the start (לכתחילה).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן could say to you: here, where the משנה teaches "One may not roof with them," it is speaking about what to do from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to defend רבי יוחנן against רב אשי by pointing to the exact words of the משנה. The answer continues past the end of this passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אין מסככין בהן" is softer language that only tells you not to do it in the first place. This fits a rabbinic precaution like גזירת אוצר. The grain-stack case, by contrast, says the structure is not a סוכה at all, which fits the Torah-level rule of תעשה ולא מן העשוי. That contrast is the defense. Only its first half, about the bundles, appears on this amud. The contrast with the grain-stack wording comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Could say to you. Introduces how a sage would answer the challenge.
It teaches. Refers to the wording of the משנה.
One may not use them as סכך.
From the start. Describes what one should do before acting, as opposed to judging something already done.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's choice of words ("may not roof" versus "is not a סוכה") can show how severe a rule is and where it comes from.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan could say to you,
here, where it teaches:
"One may not roof with them,"
it is speaking about what to do from the start
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud, which contrasts this with the grain-stack wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual: the different wording in the משנה shows that the two rules differ in strength.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both reasons apply equally to both cases, as רב אשי argued.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bundles rule is written only as a לכתחילה restriction, which marks it as the rabbinic גזירת אוצר. The contrast with the grain-stack case comes on the next amud.
